I'm an absolute beginner, so forgive me if this seems poorly researched. I'd like to be able to track my runs, my progress, set goals and input my own training sessions with audio cues. I've got an Android phone, so I'd like to be able to continue using that platform if possible. I've looked at the popular search results, things like Runkeeper, Runtastic, Strava, etc. and it seems like each has a feature I'd like to use, but requires a subscription that frankly seems ridiculous at $20-40 a year to store a tiny bit of data. I don't mind paying for an app, but spending $5 for an app and then an auto-renewing $30+ a year feels like joining a scammy gym.

Are there any less-popular apps that you guys and gals are aware of that have some useful features but don't require a subscription and my first-born?
Using MyTracks to log myself, but looking for something better. Help?
Did you try mapmyrun? I use mapmybike and I like it, I assume mmr is pretty similar.
I didn't try it, but I did look into it. As per the Play page and their MVP site, it appears audio cues and training sessions are a $30/year feature. App looks nice, though.

I wish I could help you, but I use a Garmin watch to track all my fitness stuff. I like it because it is a one time purchase and then you get access to their tools forever. I'm not sure which watch would have all the features you are looking for - but it might be something you could look into.

I have the Garmin FR620 - which is fantastic (but probably total overkill for what you are looking for). They have several watches that are under $100.

Thanks, @ghallo, I'll take your recommendations and put 'em up on the bookshelf for now. To be perfectly honest, I'm still in that stage where I'm trying to convince myself that I actually enjoy running. I hear tales of the runners of yore that there comes a magical time where suddenly you actually do enjoy it - and when that time comes I think I'll feel better about purchasing something like that.

Until then, if you pass a bald guy who doesn't say hello, don't take it personally - it's probably just me, gasping for air. :)

Running isn't usually fun "during". Well, sometimes it is. Usually it is the afterglow.

For me its fun during with the rare exception (as long as Im not trying to be fast, anyway!)

I second Garmin - the initial investment is high, but Im very happy with all the Connect software. I recently upgraded my FR220 to the FR920XT (my 220 still works fine but the battery life wasnt enough for my slow-ass 12hour 50mile time).

I really enjoy Strava. I've used it with a phone, several Garmin devices, and my Suunto Ambit 3. It works flawlessly with all devices.

It is free, but you do have the option to pay if you'd like to use a few other features.
